page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine featuring a dedicated Intel Xeon CPU with 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores, 2 threads per core) running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory and includes a bundled NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not included with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates a clear division in performance capabilities. Standard CPU-bound tasks, memory bandwidth, and general-purpose operations—such as stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark CPU tests—consistently rank in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. However, the integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance for specialized workloads. Large Language Model (LLM) inference benchmarks for both small (135M) and medium (7B) models place this instance in the top 10% for prompt processing and text generation speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-4 offers a specialized entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads without the overhead of larger multi-GPU configurations. While standard compute and memory resources are modest, the inclusion of 24 GB of VRAM makes it highly cost-effective for machine learning inference, small-to-medium model deployment, and graphics rendering. It is less suitable for CPU-heavy tasks, database hosting, or high-throughput web serving due to its lower general-purpose benchmark scores.

This hardware profile makes the g2-standard-4 highly efficient for specialized workloads such as AI inference, graphics rendering, and low-latency model deployment, while serving as a less optimal choice for general-purpose compute or database operations.
